parts.spokenText: A predator may consume many prey over its life. Efficient uptake combined with removal that is slow relative to intake can produce a higher tissue concentration. But not every chemical behaves this way. Chemical form, metabolism, diet and tissue basis all matter. There is no universal rule that residues increase by ten percent at every trophic level. Energy transfer is not a fixed equation for predicting a chemical concentration.

parts.spokenText: Before reading a property table, establish chemical identity, form and purity. Stereochemical forms may differ in behavior or activity, and a formulation is not necessarily equivalent to a pure substance in a laboratory test. Solubility values need temperature, pH and method information. Vapour pressure informs volatility under stated conditions. Molecular weight or any single property cannot predict the entire environmental fate. Every value needs its measurement context.
